text:
alice: Quick follow-up on the RFC — proposing we add a circuit-breaker + async prober stage to the model onboarding pipeline. Goals: keep bad models from flapping into prod, avoid false positives due to transient infra noise. Link to RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfc/1234 :thinking:

ben: I like a 2-stage prober: a lightweight latency smoke on admit, and a deep accuracy/quality prober running async. Fast probe should be cheap and deterministic (<= ~50ms median on healthy infra), deep probe can be heavier and revoke admission if it finds regressions.

caro: +1. For the fast probe use a tiny set of golden prompts (short seeds) focusing on latency-sensitive tokens. Deep probe should run a 200-example eval and compute diffs. Keep both results in registry.

diego: Circuit-breaker idea: token-bucket style but based on sliding-window SLO breaches. Something like: trip if p99 latency > 1.5x expected for 5 out of 6 windows of 60s. Also limit auto-rollbacks to X per day to avoid thrashing.

frank: Also include a KV-cache warmup step in probes, otherwise first-call latency will spike and look like a regression. e.g. `warm_kv: true` before measuring.

alice: Good call on warmup. One more: fallback chain — auto-degrade to quantized variant, then to smaller model. But we need to track output drift and surface that to the team.

ben: :thumbsup: Fallbacks are fine but be careful on quality regressions. Deep prober should compute a quality_delta and if > 0.05 trigger rollback.

caro: Draft config snippet for discussion:

```yaml
circuit_breaker:
  window_seconds: 60
  p99_threshold_ms: 1500
  breach_count_to_trip: 5
  cool_down_seconds: 300
probers:
  fast:
    sample_prompts: 10
    max_latency_ms: 200
    warm_kv: true
  deep:
    sample_prompts: 200
    quality_delta_threshold: 0.05
    run_frequency_minutes: 30
fallback_policy:
  - variant: quantized
  - variant: smaller_model_x2
```

diego: Concern: noisy p99s during infra maintenance might cause unwanted trips. Circuit-breaker should consult cluster-health signals and host maintenance tags before tripping.

alice: Agreed. Also add a `force_admit` flag for SEs to override for experiments — but it must be audited and limited to specific users.

onboard-bot: smoke-prober: run for `model-abc` completed — fast_probe: pass, deep_probe: scoring pending.

frank: We should persist the last N probe results in the model registry with a TTL (24h). UI should expose last 3 diffs + trend sparkline.

caro: Testing plan suggestion: canary at 1% traffic with prober gating enabled. Measure user-facing latency delta and compare with and without fallback.

ben: Ops callout — different policies for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private. Private deployments must not auto-fallback without explicit customer opt-in. Add a policy flag.

alice: Good catch. Default auto-fallback = hosted only. For Private deployments, require customer approval and CS ticketing.

diego: I'll open a follow-up RFC for the telemetry schema (probe results, drift metrics, circuit events) and incident bot integration.

alice: Next steps: diego -> RFC telemetry + incident hooks; ben -> implement config + unit tests; caro -> prober harness + golden sets; frank -> UI artifact for probe history. We'll sync in one week. :eyes:

onboard-bot: deploy-bot: branch `feature/onboard-prober` merged to staging; deploy scheduled.

ben: ack

caro: ack

frank: ack
